Look, we can animate! Don't pay attention to the consecutively disappointing, recycled tropes and plot holes though ^^ Looks pretty, right? Now the best thing is that you are going to eat it up because it is Spiderman!! And because it is Spiderman you don't even have to think for yourself because the plot is being spoon-fed to you, isn't that great? Look at our other movies that have the exact same character arc again and again all over!!! And we even have super hip music that you guys at your age enjoy! You're going to love it!! Rant : It seems that in general, people justify this audiovisual product by saying: "Oh, but it looks pretty!" I have a few problems with this. First of all, this kind of animation is also from the perspective of 2018 nowhere near revolutionary. It is not daring of them "to try a new style" since typical marvel fans are just eating everything up anyway. And it's marvel, they can afford it. This movie just wanted to be edgy but in the end produced the same recycled and overused marvel tropes as always. "It was my fault" before the random ass villain uncle dies, the shy new kid at school, main character suddenly gaining confidence and being able to do crazy things even though they couldn't do anything before.. Aunt May being in on the secret just for convenience's sake to keep the plot going? Also, how ironic that trying to force your movie to be self-aware about it's overused tropes just sheds more light on HOW OVERUSED YOUR TROPES ARE. It's like shooting yourself in the knee and laughing awkwardly while doing it. Half of the things that happened had no significance because, guess what? There was a magic USB-Stick that happened to have the perfect code to stop the big evil machine from blowing everything up, wow how convenient for the main character, he didn't even have to do anything... Oh, and the music felt insulting to my ears.

At least it looks good? That is the nicest thing I can say about it, and it is doing a lot of heavy lifting. The whole thing feels like a gacha game. Gorgeous art and not much going on underneath. I am not trying to be edgy here. I am a mild Marvel fan, I went in wanting to like it, and it still felt like an insult to my intelligence. The characters have almost no depth. I get that it is 105 minutes and the first in a series, but some kind of motivation would have been nice. Kingpin wants his family back and that is the entire plot I guess? The other spider people show up so late and do so little that they might as well be alternate skins. Peni and Spider-Ham exist for one joke each. Gwen gets a haircut and that's basically it? Then there is the plot, where things happen because they have to happen. This is unfair hindsight, but No Way Home does the same setup and at least tries to make it hold together. Here it just occurs. Aunt May knows science now and has a secret lab. Miles' uncle happens to be a major villain, gets one scene of weight, and then immediately dies. Miles can do nothing for an hour and then can do everything after a montage. I am not asking for Stephen King level writing. It is basically a kids movie. But when everything just happens, there is nothing solid enough to even have an opinion about. Every emotional moment gets undermined by a joke before it lands, so even the sad parts feel like they are not being taken seriously. I am just dissapointed that the sometimes gorgeous visuals are not backed up by a story that is even 10% as good at them I cannot fully explain it. This movie just makes me angry.

No idea, sure he saw his masked weirdo get killed in front of him, but others came, other that were far more capable that were not keen on having dead weight to lug around. The idea of not doing schoolwork was part of his plan, but bailing on being Spiderman wasn't. Is that his motivation, looking cool? Why was he so eager to get the Spider-people's approval? Miles' story is that of an uncomplicated character: he gets everything, does the right thing and the only blemish is his character is the fact that he idolised a crook. I wondered if I would like this more on rewatch. When I watched this the first time, I probably had a lot of Marvel fatigue, and I liked Across the Spider-Verse a lot since. But I think this is a tough rewatch as well as a tough thing to watch after having watched... even more Marvel stuff, including Deadpool & Wolverine. I want to get the most technical problem I have out of the way, though: for as innovative and psychedelic as this animation is, I think it's hard to look at sometimes. Visually, there are just too many ideas and not all of them work. The "halftone shader"? Love it. The chromatic aberration effects? They get a little distracting sometimes. The way they render depth of field? Hate it. When they are running out of the lab through the cafeteria, there is a shot that begins only with scientists sitting at a table out of focus (because our heroes aren't in frame yet). It looks horrible. When anything is very out of focus, it looks horrible. (I don't recall having these quibbles with Across; I assume without reading my review that they ironed out the kinks of this aesthetic.) Now, not unlike the look, the story and its comedy both have moments while also having problems. My problems with the story are enormous in 2026, and it's a testament to what I do like about this movie that it gets a positive score from me. Because... if I really had to say, I would say I do not like this movie. It's just so... I'm sorry, it's just so Marvel. Self-congratulatory IP-waving? Check. Bad science fiction? Check. Unwelcome self-reflexive glibness? Check. Unrelatably high stakes? Check. I have gone from having a distaste for these qualities in Marvel stories to simply not tolerating them. I remember being bummed on my first viewing of this movie that it felt like it ended on a hamfisted "and you could be Spider-Man too, so care about him and his many revenue-generating incarnations, please" note. I completely forgot that it's way more crass up front. The early character development in this movie is not Miles Morales as Spider-Man or Peter Parker as Spider-Man or a different Peter Parker as Spider-Man. It's Spider-Man as intellectual property. And it's not like other superhero fiction hasn't done this. I know specifically of Superman and Wonder Woman fiction that acknowledges their celebrity in-world, even going so far as to include comic books of these characters (like this movie does). But the ends justify the means so much better in those stories. This just feels like Marvel reminding you of how big Spider-Man is in our world, not his own. Because the Spider-Man of this movie's (main) world is one of two people. It's Peter Parker, who died early and isn't established all that well in any real detail. Again, he and every other Spider-Man are overshadowed by Spider-Man (tm). Or, it's Miles Morales, who gets Spider-Mogged in his own movie. I just find his arc to be really unsatisfying: he's bad at Spider-Stuff until he's pretty suddenly not and... Guys, this plot is all and only about fixing and inserting a USB drive (which Sweatpants Peter himself mocks in typical Marvel movie fashion... guys, if you want to talk me into the idea that your movie is bad, don't be upset when I agree with you). Bad. Science. Fiction. And we run away from all of Miles's worldly relationships immediately in order to remedy multiversal concerns of little tangibility (though they do try to humanize Kingpin and it's more convincing than it has much right to be). Furthermore, when you blast past reality with that much impatience, I begin to have my own impatience about your inability to tell stories about heroism that have any real-life connections. We do not need superheroes to model how to act in the face of a supercollider when we've fallen on the magical thumb drive that saves the world. We need models of actual interpersonal bravery and compassion (but then again I would say that as a Wonder Woman fan), for when we're challenged with much more likely problems. Look. It has moments and a groundbreaking (if flawed) look. But, again... it's just SO Marvel. And I'm really, really tired of that tone and those problems that are so common to these stories. Next time you consume a Marvel story, I want you to try something. Ask "what if I didn't care about the most extremely made-up parts of this?" I think it makes these stories fall apart really often and reveals how much Marvel expects us to just buy in as a matter of course. I think you see this attitude in the way they flex Spider-Man as IP here and do an MCU victory lap around the X-Men movies (which have rich stories apart from the mutations) in Deadpool & Wolverine. This movie is about Spider-Man (tm), not Miles Morales. I wish I'd learned more about him, what he cares about, and the people who live on the same Earth as him. And I don't think these are unreasonable demands to make on a story.

Au niveau de l'intrigue par contre c'est moins bien de manière générale, bien que je trouve le début avec la mort de Peter Parker assez réussie, la suite va vraiment être un peu trop basique à mon gout. Il y a d'abord l'antagoniste qui a mon sens n'a qu'un proto-développement un peu bâclé, des facilités un peu grossières comme la meuf spiderman qui est dans le labo et qui arrive à la rescousse, c'est assez curieux. J'ai aussi trouvé qu'il y a eu un certain manque de progressivité dans le power up de Miles, genre il passe vraiment du tout au tout sans transition, sans vraiment se découvrir. Bref, l'histoire bien que trop basique se regarde bien grâce aux touches d'humour et l'animation originale. Un bon moment.
